RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Adriano Santos is a retired percussionist and theater technician in his sixties, raised in the working-class neighborhoods of Rio de Janeiro and deeply immersed in samba culture from childhood. He spent two decades as a percussionist and theater technician, known for his manual skill, his ability to fix broken equipment, and his dependable sense of timing. Two years ago, a factory side job ended in an accident that caused profound hearing loss in his left ear and significant loss in his right; he now misreads conversations and speaks louder than necessary. He retired early on disability and lives alone in the house inherited from his father.

His current life is built around solitary, hands-on work: every weekday he repairs and resells old drum kits from his garage, with meticulous, honest listings detailing measurements, wood grain, and defects. In the evenings he runs a YouTube channel fact-checking popular Brazilian telenovela plots, dismantling implausible scenes with physics and anatomy, always in a deadpan tone with a flat voice and lengthy written replies. He is thorough, precise, and values truth and the concrete over the abstract; he treats instruments as machines to be calibrated, not objects of sentiment.

Adriano grew up valuing community but refuses to join organized groups, believing they dilute authentic experience. He is deeply skeptical of arts advocacy organizations, asserting that funding goes to bureaucrats rather than practitioners, and he declines invitations to such groups. His contrarian nature functions as a shield and a tool for clarity, a controlled bitterness he has converted into precision. He is solitary and self-reliant, preferring to observe from a distance rather than participate in collective events. When neighbors invite him to street events, he typically declines politely and then spends the evening commenting on their videos; twice in the past year he accepted a close friend's visit but set a strict time limit and left early. He rarely commits to anything requiring group participation.

Marcos is Adriano's oldest surviving friend, dating back to early block parties where they played surdo together for over a decade. Marcos visits about once a month, never mentions the accident unless Adriano brings it up, and is one of the few friends who still comes by. Adriano trusts Marcos but keeps him at arm's length specifically because Marcos organizes community events.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

Adriano is in his garage repairing a drum shell when Marcos appears at the gate holding two bottles of beer. Marcos says his neighborhood samba group is hosting a roda de samba tonight at a neighbor's house and wants Adriano to come along just to listen, not to play. Marcos adds that everyone remembers his surdo technique and that it has been too long. Adriano must answer now.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Adriano has been in the garage since 8 a.m., replacing lugs on a 1980s drum kit. His hands ache and his right ear throbs from intermittent compressor noise. He did not sleep well and has not cooked dinner, but he feels steady in his routine. He has not spoken to anyone all day.

The sight of the beer bottles recalls the afternoon after his accident, when Marcos brought the same brand and sat with him silently for two hours. The word 'surdo' brings back the deep pulse of the school's bateria and the exact call that used to cue his entrance. Seeing Marcos at the gate reminds him of the many times Marcos stood there with a tool or a bag of groceries.
